title: nearby-fauna.csv distances are kilometres labelled as miles
description:
tools/fetch-nearby-fauna.mjs:132 passes RADII_MI straight to the iNaturalist species_counts 'radius' param. That param is in KM, not miles — tools/fetch-ecosystem-index.mjs:317 already knows this and multiplies by MI_TO_KM.

Verified live against the backyard coordinates (2026-09-13), Aves:
  radius=3      -> 166 species
  radius=4.828  -> 330 species   (3 mi expressed in km)

So every 'nearest_radius_mi' value in ecology/nearby-fauna.csv is really a kilometre figure: the '3 mi' band actually covered 1.86 mi, and each band holds roughly half the species it should.

Two consequences:
1. src/analysis/faunaMatches.js RANGE_THRESHOLD_MI compares miles against kilometres, so inRange is wrong.
2. Anything rendering 'confirmed within N mi' overstates the distance.

Fix: convert in fetch-nearby-fauna.mjs the same way fetch-ecosystem-index.mjs does, then re-fetch. Found while adding establishment_means to the same file.
close_reason: Closed

title: Un-pin / condense the sticky toolbar on mobile
description:
styles.css:56 sets .view-toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0 }. Measured 547px tall at 412px wide = 60% of a 915px viewport and ~70% of a real Pixel 10's ~780px visible area. Confirmed pinning at top:0 across scrollY 400-1200, i.e. the entire range where any view is on screen. Usable height below it is 368px measured, ~233px on device - less than the 278px height of a single .view. The app's only content cannot fit on screen.

It stacks, vertically, at 412px: legend (3 items), 5 layer chips wrapping to 3 ragged right-aligned rows (105px), 2 pill switches + Undo/Redo, month label+slider+readout, scale label+slider+number input, and a 3-bar 'Scale reference' card with a hint line.
design:
Options:
- Drop position:sticky below ~960px, or keep only a ~56px condensed bar (month scrubber + a 'Controls' button) pinned and move the rest into a bottom sheet / <details> drawer.
- The month slider is the core interaction and the one control worth permanent space. Scale, layers, labels, lock, undo/redo and the legend are set-once-then-forget.
- Move the legend and 'Scale reference' card below the views or into the drawer.
- Collapse the scale row: #scaleInput duplicates #scaleSlider, and each view already renders its own '1 ft = N px' badge (.view-scale).
acceptance_criteria: At 412x915, a complete .view is visible on screen at the same time as whatever toolbar remains pinned.

title: Tap a plant to open a species detail sheet
description:
On mobile there is no way to see species details by touch. Provable from source; a resized desktop browser has hover and will falsely appear to work.

- Details are delivered ONLY through native SVG <title> tooltips (src/render/tooltip.js -> renderTopView / renderElevationView). Confirmed 192 <title> elements for 192 plant groups. <title> never fires on touch.
- styles.css reinforces this with '.view svg [data-name]:hover { cursor: pointer }'.
- Species table cross-highlighting is bound to mouseenter/mouseleave (src/app.js:734-735) - hover-only.
- Clone is bound to contextmenu (src/app.js:522), and a document click handler at :541 hides the menu. Android long-press over SVG should be verified on-device rather than assumed, but there is no discoverable tap affordance either way.

Net: tapping a plant on a phone does nothing. The species table at the bottom of a 7-screen page is the only route to details and is disconnected from the plant you tapped.
design:
Add a click/pointerup handler on [data-plant-id] that opens a bottom sheet rendering buildTooltipLines(plant, state), plus a 'Clone' action - this reuses the existing tooltip builder and replaces the contextmenu-only clone path with something that works on both input types. Mirror mouseenter/mouseleave on species rows with click-to-pin highlighting. Keep the <title> elements: they remain the desktop tooltip and the accessible name.

Blast radius (codegraph impact buildTooltipLines): tooltip.js, topView.js, elevationViews.js, renderViews.js, tests/topView.test.js, tests/elevationViews.test.js.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping a plant in any of the three views opens a detail sheet with the same content the desktop tooltip shows, and offers Clone. No regression to the existing <title> tooltips.
close_reason: tap [data-plant-id] opens a bottom detail sheet (buildTooltipLines content) with a Clone action; verified via headless iframe at 412x915, existing SVG <title> tooltips unaffected

title: touch-action:none while unlocked swallows page scroll over every view
description:
src/interaction/dragController.js:170 and :349 set svg.style.touchAction = locked ? 'auto' : 'none'. Verified: with positions unlocked, all three view SVGs compute touch-action:none.

Each view is 370x278 inside a 412px column, so any vertical swipe that STARTS on a drawing is swallowed and the page will not scroll. With three views stacked, most of the scrollable area is dead. This is the single most maddening mobile behavior in the app, and is half the reason the scrolling feels 'nested'.

Locked is the default (lockToggle checked, no localStorage on first visit), so a first-time visitor will not hit this - but it makes editing on a phone effectively impossible.
design:
Either:
- use touch-action: pan-y instead of none while unlocked, so vertical page scroll survives and drags read as horizontal/hold gestures; or
- require a long-press (or tap-to-select-then-drag) to begin a touch drag, keeping touch-action:auto until that gesture is recognized.

Blast radius (codegraph impact createPlantDragController): dragController.js, src/app.js init.
acceptance_criteria: With positions unlocked on a touch device, a vertical swipe starting on a drawing scrolls the page, and dragging a plant still works.
close_reason: touch-action: pan-y instead of none, preserves vertical page scroll while unlocked

title: PLANTS spine REPLACES the hex map as the homepage lead
description:
AUTHORITATIVE WORDING, revised by the owner 2026-09-16. Supersedes the earlier draft and closed issue nl-3hi.9.

 P - Plant natives that fit your site
 L - Leave the leaves, stems, and seed heads
 A - Avoid pesticides
 N - No invasives
 T - Trees first, especially native oaks
 S - Something blooming or fruiting every season

PROVENANCE: Claude-generated, not a published framework. It has no citation AS A MNEMONIC and must not be presented as 'from the research'. Label it a packaging of the literature - a memory aid - and cite each letter individually. An untested acronym also has no validation as a behaviour-change tool; stay humble given the finding that information alone rarely shifts yard behaviour.

WHAT THE REVISION FIXED:
 - P dropped 'mostly (aim for about 70% of plant mass)'. That number was the weakest item in the evidence audit and the same unreplicated Narango figure that sank the parcel map; 'plant mass' was also not homeowner-assessable and rewarded woody over herbaceous. Gone from the front page - it belongs on the reasoning page as provenance only. P now also absorbs HORTICULTURAL FIT (do not waste water on species that do not match the site).
 - L now names stems and seed heads explicitly, so it covers cavity/stem-nesting bees and winter seed as well as leaf litter. Statutory backing: Tex. Prop. Code 202.007(a)(1) protects composting vegetation and leaving grass clippings - an HOA cannot ban this outright.
 - S changed from 'Save birds: keep cats indoors and mark windows' to seasonal continuity, which gives bloomSuccession.js and birdFood.js a letter for the first time.

MAPPING TO THE EXISTING RULES ENGINE (4 of 6 letters now map, vs 2 before):
 P -> siteMatch.js + keystoneGenera.js + larvalHosts.js
 L -> no rule (management)
 A -> no rule (management)
 N -> dfw-avoid-non-natives.csv exists but is surfaced NOWHERE; no rule
 T -> verticalLayers.js + keystoneGenera.js
 S -> bloomSuccession.js + birdFood.js
Only L and A are pure behaviour with nothing computable behind them.

DEMOTED, NOT DELETED: cats indoors + marked windows left the mnemonic. They remain the BEST-EVIDENCED content available (Loss, Will & Marra 2013, Nature Communications 4:1396 - 1.3-4.0 billion US birds/yr, likely the single greatest anthropogenic source; Loss, Loss, Will & Marra 2014, The Condor 116(1) - 365-988 million/yr from building collisions, 44% at residences 1-3 stories). Owner confirmed earlier they want this on the site. Keep it as a companion surface beside L and A - things you DO rather than things you PLANT - and do not bury it. Carry the honesty notes: state the per-yard rate alongside the national aggregate, and say plainly that one indoor-kept cat outweighs one marked window.

title: Part Two's NWF headline is refutable in 30 seconds - rescope it to the printed PDF
description:

NWF's zip-code Native Plant Finder (https://nativeplantfinder.nwf.org/about) states results 'are based on the historic native ranges of plants as determined by the USDA NRCS Plant Database, which are based on range maps that go down to the county level' and will 'only show native plants that were historically present in your county'. The foil must be named precisely: the PRINTED Level I ecoregion-9 keystone PDF (the thing handed out at plant sales), not 'NWF's data'. Copy must acknowledge the county tool exists, or a reader checks the zip tool, sees no larch, and dismisses the whole screen.

title: Pivot: from scoring parcels to surfacing what's needed and what's nearby
description:
SUPERSEDES the earlier plan recorded here (three interactive taxon hex layers + a graded/binary parcel-goodness map). Retired 2026-09-16 at the owner's direction; the reasoning below is why, and is worth keeping.

WHY THE PARCEL-GOODNESS MAP IS CUT. It stacked three unvalidated layers:
 1. the 70% native-biomass threshold - single-site, single-species, unreplicated (Narango, Tallamy & Marra 2018, PNAS 115(45))
 2. the parcels -> biomass-fraction conversion - NO published mapping exists at all
 3. a habitat scoring rubric - the category of instrument that empirically FAILED field validation (Garfinkel et al. 2023, Ecological Indicators 148:110062: 'the pollinator habitat score was not a significant predictor of bee and lepidopteran pollinator biodiversity')
And its output was actionable by nobody: no individual controls a hex. Most speculative thing on the site AND the least useful.

WHAT REPLACES IT - observational, not modelled:
 - habitat ANCHORS (creeks, parks, preserves, remnant prairie, cemeteries, utility easements) and distance to them = facts
 - what is already NEARBY = already built (iNaturalist, ecology/nearby-fauna.csv, ecosystem drawer)
 - what is MISSING in your yard = derived from plants.csv (growth_shape, height_ft, flowering_season_months give layer occupancy + bloom continuity)
 - what to PLANT = Part Two's FNCT-cited screen, the strongest asset on the site
 - PLANTS mnemonic as the prioritisation spine (see child issue)

HARD BOUNDARY: do NOT emit a connectivity score, gradient, or weighted lines. Anchor location and distance are facts; 'how connected you are' is a model, and scoring it rebuilds the parcel map with new geometry and none of the epistemic gain. Show distance and NAME what lies between (road, highway, continuous turf). Stop there.

STILL VALID from the earlier plan:
 - DECISION 0 = (B): index.html goes homeowner-facing; the three asks move to the reasoning page.
 - DECISION 4: no exclusion anywhere. No 'wrong street'. (Page never did say it - verified in verdictText.)
 - DECISION 6: reasoning gets its own page + nav entry.
 - DECISION 5 = (b) then (c), filed separately and unaffected.
 - The ADJACENCY TAXONOMY survives as EXPLANATION on the reasoning page, not as interactive geometry: birds = adjacency as DENSITY (fraction of a ~1-2ha window); bees = CO-LOCATION (forage + nesting substrate + bloom continuity within ~150m); herps = TOPOLOGY (unbroken passable path; fences and roads are hard barriers). Bee citations: Hofmann, Fleischmann & Renner 2020 (J. Hym. Res., 6-15mm bees, mean female flight 73-121m); Greenleaf et al. 2007 (Oecologia 153:589-596, range scales with body size). The urban literature is SPLIT (local-dominates: PLOS One 2024, Landscape Ecology 2025; isolation-matters: PubMed 40947939) - the reconciliation that the suburban matrix saturates the forage term is MY judgement call, not any paper's, and must be labelled as such per the repo's own convention.
 - Lepidoptera deliberately not a separate layer: Part Two IS the lep layer.

DEAD: three interactive hex views; any per-parcel score.

title: Name reconciliation is a prerequisite for every book-sourced field
description:
MEASURED on nl-41o.3: 119 of 469 rows in blackland-prairie-natives.csv matched no
treatment in the NCTX flora. The verified cause is 1999 NOMENCLATURE, not absence
-- Symphyotrichum oblongifolium is treated, as Aster oblongifolius.

Until a catalog name can be resolved to the name set a 1999 source uses, "not
found" is uninterpretable: it conflates renamed-since with genuinely-absent. That
makes it impossible to distinguish "the flora is silent, so native by convention"
from "we failed to look it up" -- and collapsing the two is exactly how
non-natives get silently promoted into recommendations.

USDA PLANTS publishes synonyms (field 17 in doc 01) and is the obvious source.
Sized as its own bead because it gates the flora, gates any future book source,
and is not specific to either.

Also measured: a binomial-only match misses infraspecific taxa entirely
(Bothriochloa ischaemum var. songarica read as absent though it is treated), and
this repo's catalogs are full of var./subsp. names -- Malvaviscus arboreus var.
drummondii, Achillea millefolium var. occidentalis, Anisacanthus quadrifidus var.
wrightii. Reconciliation has to handle rank, not just the binomial.

See docs/data-acquisition/03-document-corpus.md §5.
close_reason: Wrote docs/data-acquisition/06-name-reconciliation.md: rank-aware name reconciliation algorithm (flora's own in-text synonym crosswalk preferred over USDA PlantSynonyms round-trip), validated live against the Symphyotrichum/Aster oblongifolius case and USDA id 40799's synonym set.

title: Working source-probe MCP tools, for use during the analysis
description:
Build phase 1 of the introspection surface (nl-41o.8) as a REAL, USABLE tool,
early, so the investigation beads are done with instruments rather than by hand.

This is the one IMPLEMENTATION bead in an otherwise analysis-only epic, and it
is deliberate. nl-41o.1 has to answer "does any source publish this field at
county granularity" for dozens of fields, and nl-41o.2 has to verify coverage
and access claims across a dozen sources. Doing that by reading documentation
produces beliefs; doing it with a probe produces measurements. The tool pays for
itself inside the epic that specifies it.

Scope is deliberately small: probe a source, show what came back, report which
required fields it populated. No claim store, no writes, no persistence beyond
a cache. Everything else waits for nl-41o.8 and nl-41o.4.
design:
BUILD ONLY PHASE 1 from nl-41o.8: source probe, field sniff, run state.
Resist the rest — coverage and provenance need the claim store and building
them against a guess at the model will have to be redone.

STARTING POINT: the usda-plants MCP server already exists and is wired into the
session (usda_search_by_location, usda_search_by_name, usda_fetch_details,
usda_download_plant_list). Decide whether this extends it or sits beside it;
nl-41o.8 flags that two servers with overlapping vocabulary is the bad outcome.

WHAT MAKES IT USEFUL RATHER THAN A DETOUR:
  - RAW output, not a normalized view. The whole point is seeing what the source
    actually said, so a parse bug is distinguishable from a source gap. The Alnus
    case from nl-jsm.1 is the precedent: a clean-looking extraction silently
    dropped a row and only a second view of the same document caught it.
  - Cache responses. The availability audit will probe the same species
    repeatedly across several sittings, and re-fetching is slow and rude to the
    source.
  - Report per-field population against the required-fields list from nl-41o.1,
    once that list exists. Before it exists, probe against the fields already
    known missing: county nativity, soil/light/water tolerance, mature width,
    commercial availability.

NOT IN SCOPE: writing anything into plants.csv or any claim store. This tool
reads and reports. Collection is a later epic.
acceptance_criteria:
• Probe returns a source's RAW response for a species, without normalizing it
• Reports which of the target fields that source populated for that species
• Responses cached, so a repeated probe does not re-fetch
• Extends or sits beside the existing usda-plants server, with the choice
  recorded and no overlapping tool vocabulary
• Read-only: no path from this tool to a committed data file
notes:
NOT a gate on nl-41o.1/.2 — deliberately. Those two and this one INTERLEAVE: .1 names a required field, this probes whether a source publishes it, the answer sharpens .1's availability audit, repeat. A hard dependency either way would be wrong, since this bead's own design consumes .1's field list while .1's availability half consumes this bead's output. Start with the fields already known missing (county nativity, soil/light/water tolerance, mature width, commercial availability) and let the list grow.
TOOLING (decided on the epic 2026-08-27): built in NODE, extending tools/usda-plants
rather than sitting beside it — that settles this bead's open question about extend
vs adjacent, and satisfies nl-41o.8's one-vocabulary rule. Cache backed by SQLite
(node:sqlite, built in — no dependency).
PROBE TARGETS, ordered by cost-of-being-wrong (from nl-41o.1):
1. BONAP — county nativity, and on what terms. The one unresolved blocker.
2. The distribution endpoint AT SCALE. nl-41o.1 measured 4 species; confirm it holds for
   several hundred and establish a polite rate. One POST per species = ~500 requests for
   the Blackland list. Endpoint:
   POST /api/PlantProfile/getDownloadDistributionDocumentation {"masterId": <id>}
3. LBJ NPIN — regional bloom/fruit timing and mature width (the non-book candidate for
   the width gap).
4. The other 55 USDA characteristics — nl-41o.1 sampled ONE species (Quercus shumardii).
   Confirm the useful ones are populated broadly, not just for a well-studied oak.
CAUTION to carry into any new source: mapCharacteristics.js:96-113 documents that USDA's
live Shade Tolerance values run OPPOSITE to its own Swagger enum (verified 14/15 vs 0/15).
That inversion already caused commit ed9d75c. Check any light field the same way before
trusting it.
PROBE TARGETS REVISED after nl-41o.2. BONAP is DONE — do not spend probe effort there;
its terms answer the question and the blocker is legal, not technical.
New ordering:
1. /api/characteristicSearchResults and /api/characteristicSearchResultsDownload — a
   DIFFERENT bulk path from the plants-search-results one known to time out. If either
   works it replaces per-species fetching wholesale. Cheapest high-upside probe available.
2. NPIN AT VOLUME — does per-species retrieval hold beyond three pages, and at what rate?
   Measured working with a browser UA on CHLI2/QUSH/ILVO. Pair with an EMAIL to the Center,
   since the terms page is the one thing Cloudflare blocks. Do not work around it.
3. NPIN larval-host and light-set COVERAGE — found on 2 of 2 species examined. If broadly
   populated, these are the fields that un-stick R5 and R8's light check.
4. GBIF county filtering via GADM — a licence-tagged second opinion on county presence.
5. /api/PlantWildlife fill rate (carried over from nl-41o.1).
close_reason: Built usda_probe / usda_probe_target_fields (extends tools/usda-plants, one vocabulary per the epic's rule): raw profile+characteristics for one species, cached in data/probe-cache.db (node:sqlite), sniffed against county-nativity/soil-light-water-tolerance/mature-width/commercial-availability. Field sniff is honest by construction: near-miss key matches (measured live: 'Seed Spread Rate' matches a width regex on Quercus shumardii) are surfaced as a diagnostic for human review, never auto-adopted as a value; characteristicsCount distinguishes a zero-record taxon from a real per-field gap.

title: MCP interface for pipeline introspection
description:
Design the MCP surface an agent uses to watch and steer the collection as it
runs — not just to read the finished data.

The existing usda-plants MCP tools fetch. That is enough to pull a record and
not enough to answer "why does this species have no soil tolerance", "what did
this source actually return for it", "which claim won this field and what lost",
or "what is left to collect". Without those, every diagnosis means re-running
the pipeline by hand and reading its output, which is slow and does not compose.

Design only. The tools this names are built with the pipeline, not before it.
design:
PHASED DELIBERATELY, because most of this needs no data model and waiting for
one would keep the tooling away from exactly the work it makes faster. Only the
claim-store queries depend on nl-41o.4; everything else can be designed and used
before it exists. See nl-41o.9, which builds the first phase as a working tool
to be used DURING the investigation beads.

PHASE 1 — needs nothing but a source. Usable while doing nl-41o.1/.2/.3.
  Source probe   What a given source returns for a given species, RAW, without
                 committing it. The way to tell a bad parse from a bad source
                 without polluting anything. This is also how the availability
                 audit in nl-41o.1 gets answered per field rather than assumed,
                 and how the licensing/coverage claims in nl-41o.2 get checked
                 rather than taken from documentation.
  Field sniff    For one species, which of the required fields does this source
                 actually populate? Turns "USDA has soil tolerance" from a
                 belief into a measurement.
  Run state      What is queued, in flight, failed, rate-limited; what a retry
                 would do.

PHASE 2 — needs the claim store from nl-41o.4.
  Coverage       What is missing, sliced by species / field / source. Both the
                 quality report and the work queue; one query serving both is
                 the point.
  Provenance     For one species x field: every claim, its source, retrieval
                 time, confidence, which won and WHY. The 'why' matters — a
                 precedence rule that cannot be explained cannot be debugged.
  Conflicts      Unadjudicated disagreements, plus a path to record a correction
                 through the same interface. Per nl-41o.5 a correction needs a
                 reason and an author, so the tool must demand both.
  Dry run        What a collection pass WOULD change, before it changes it.

DESIGN NOTES:
  - Read tools and write tools are different risk classes. A correction is a
    write and should look like one.
  - Return shapes small and composable. codegraph_explore is the good local
    model: one call answers the whole question instead of a dozen round trips.
  - Introspection must not require the pipeline to be running.
  - Some of this deserves a human-facing view in the app, not only an agent tool.

CHECK FIRST what the existing usda-plants MCP server already offers
(usda_search_by_location, usda_search_by_name, usda_fetch_details,
usda_download_plant_list) and whether it is extended or joined by a second
server. Two servers with overlapping vocabulary would be worse than one.
acceptance_criteria:
• A named tool per capability area, with arguments and return shape
• Read and write tools clearly separated, corrections requiring reason + author
• A decision on extending the existing usda-plants server vs adding one
• A note on which introspection deserves a human-facing view, not just a tool

Read/write separated (claims_correct is the sole write tool, reason+author required); claims_coverage and claims_conflicts flagged for a human-facing view; server stays named usda-plants, reasoned explicitly.

title: Data model: species identity, claims, and provenance
description:
Design the model the collected data lands in, and the indexing that serves it.

Two hard parts:

IDENTITY. Which rows are the same plant? Synonyms are not an edge case here —
Packera obovata / Senecio obovatus already broke a rule in the shipped epic and
needed a synonym_of column to fix. Varieties (Cercis canadensis var. texensis),
cultivars ('Oklahoma', 'Nana', 'Undaunted'), and hybrids all need a position.

CLAIMS. A field is not a value, it is a value ASSERTED BY A SOURCE. Two sources
disagreeing is normal and must be representable without one silently
overwriting the other. That shape is what makes provenance, confidence,
conflict resolution, and quality metrics possible at all — get it wrong and
every one of those becomes impossible downstream.
design:
IDENTITY — what already bites:
  - Packera obovata vs Senecio obovatus: handled today by a synonym_of column in
    ecology/host-genera.csv. Works for one genus; will not scale.
  - Cultivars: "Ilex vomitoria 'Nana'" and "Muhlenbergia reverchonii 'Undaunted'"
    are in plants.csv and in both layouts. No botanical database indexes them.
    A cultivar inherits most of its species' data and overrides some (mature
    size, most obviously — 'Nana' is 4 ft against the species' 18 ft). Decide
    whether that is inheritance, a separate row, or both.
  - Varieties: "Cercis canadensis var. texensis" — an earlier commit (e2a2391)
    already had to prefer the nominate record over unlisted varieties.

CLAIMS — the shape to settle:
  something like { species_id, field, value, source, retrieved_at, confidence }
  with the flat CSV the app reads being a DERIVED PROJECTION of the claim store,
  not the store itself. That separation is what lets a re-crawl update sources
  without destroying manual corrections.

  Decide: does the app keep reading a flat plants.csv (simple, git-diffable, and
  what every existing loader expects), with the claim store behind it? Changing
  what the app reads touches src/data/plantParser.js and everything downstream,
  so there is a real argument for keeping the projection.

INDEXING: what lookups must be fast — by species, by field, by source, by
county, by "which species have no sourced value for X" (that last one drives the
quality metrics and the work queue, so it is not optional).

CONSTRAINT: whatever is chosen must stay reviewable in a pull request. Part of
why the current CSVs work is that a human can read the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
• An identity scheme covering synonyms, varieties, and cultivars, with the
  Packera and 'Nana' cases worked through explicitly
• A claim record shape that can hold two sources disagreeing
• A decision on whether the app keeps reading a flat projection, with reasoning
• The lookups the index must serve, including "what is missing"
• A statement of how this stays reviewable in a diff
notes: Delivered docs/data-acquisition/04-data-model.md. taxa/resolves_to for synonyms+varieties+cultivars (inherit-by-default, override-explicit); claims shape with license modeled as a per-claim grant evaluated at export time (not a fixed boolean, per LBJ's project-conditional grant); three-valued status (asserted/review/unknown) for book-sourced fields; plants.csv confirmed as generated projection with parser's embedded-newline limit handled by forbidding rather than fixing; six index lookups named for nl-41o.6/nl-41o.8. Two findings surfaced during review: (1) manual corrections must live in a committed plain-text file, not just claims.db rows, since claims.db is gitignored/rebuildable and corrections have no source to rebuild from -- the file is the system of record, claims.db rows are its projection. (2) nl-c58 is now a hard prerequisite of the export design, not an unrelated bug: excluding review/unknown claims from the export only keeps unreviewed data out of the catalog if blanks render as blanks downstream, and nl-c58 shows several fields currently fabricate a default instead.
close_reason: Closed

title: Source inventory: access, coverage, and licensing
description:
Catalog every candidate source for the fields the goals analysis names, and
judge each one before any crawler is written.

Per source: what fields it covers, at what granularity, how it is accessed
(API / bulk download / crawl), rate limits, terms of use and whether
redistribution in a git repo is permitted, stability of identifiers, update
cadence, and how a fact traces back to a citable location.

Licensing is not a footnote. This repo commits its data files, so a source that
forbids redistribution can inform a value but cannot BE one — that distinction
has to be settled per source before collection, not after.
design:
CANDIDATES IDENTIFIED SO FAR (2026-08-27) — evaluate, do not assume:

  USDA PLANTS          County-level distribution — the gold standard for "does
                       this occur in Dallas County". US Government work, so
                       redistribution is likely clean. MCP tools ALREADY WIRED
                       into the session: usda_search_by_location,
                       usda_search_by_name, usda_fetch_details,
                       usda_download_plant_list. texas-usda-plants.csv suggests
                       prior work started here.
  BONAP                County maps, and distinguishes native from ADVENTIVE per
                       county — a distinction USDA blurs. Not obviously
                       machine-readable; check terms carefully.
  LBJ Wildflower Ctr   NPIN species pages: soil description, light requirement,
   (NPIN)              water use, bloom time, native distribution, and often
                       propagation and commercial availability. Already cited as
                       a second source in this repo (commit e8770ff).
  NPSOT / NCTX chapter Local recommendation lists. npsot_dfw_recommended is
                       already a column in blackland-prairie-natives.csv.
  iNaturalist          Research-grade observations within a radius of Dallas —
                       ACTUAL local occurrence rather than range-map inference.
                       Has an API. Consider as corroboration, not primary.
  NWF Keystone lists   Already in use (ecology/host-genera.csv). Genus x
                       ecoregion only; note the extraction hazard documented in
                       AGENTS.md.
  Tallamy / native     Underlying host-plant research. Mostly not an API.
   plant finder
  Texas A&M AgriLife   Regional horticultural guidance, commercial availability.

Book and PDF sources are sized separately — see the pre-indexed corpus bead.

WORTH DECIDING HERE: identifier strategy. USDA symbols (CHLI2, PRAN3) already
appear in the draft CSVs and are a reasonable join key, but they do not cover
cultivars — the catalog carries "Ilex vomitoria 'Nana'" and "Muhlenbergia
reverchonii 'Undaunted'", which no botanical database indexes. Name resolution
is its own problem; it belongs to the data-model bead but the constraint is
discovered here.
acceptance_criteria:
• One row per source: fields covered, granularity, access method, rate limits,
  terms/redistribution verdict, identifier scheme, update cadence
• An explicit primary/corroborating role for each source
• A note of which required fields NO catalogued source covers
• A recommendation on the join key, and what it cannot address (cultivars)
notes:
Interleaves with nl-41o.9. Coverage and access claims taken from a source's documentation are beliefs; the same claims checked with a probe are measurements. Prefer the measurement wherever the probe can reach.
PRIORITY RAISED by nl-41o.1: BONAP is now the single unresolved blocker on the epic's
headline field. nl-41o.1 MEASURED that USDA county distribution carries no native/
adventive flag (six columns, presence only), so BONAP is the only identified candidate
for county NATIVITY. Expect the blocker to be TERMS, not access — settle the
redistribution question explicitly, because 'can inform a value but cannot BE one'
decides whether the plantable set in nl-41o.7 is definable at all.
Also revise the USDA row: county distribution IS accessible (see nl-41o.1), which
upgrades USDA's coverage claim from what tools/usda-plants/README.md records.
DELIVERABLE: docs/data-acquisition/02-source-inventory.md. Eight sources; all claims marked
MEASURED or BELIEF.

CRITICAL PATH ANSWERED — BONAP FORBIDS IT. Verbatim from http://www.bonap.org/citation.html:
'All materials on this website are copyrighted and belong to the Biota of North America
Program (BONAP). Reproduction or use of any material found on this site (e.g., distribution
maps, BIOLOGICAL ATTRIBUTE INFORMATION, images, etc.) requires advance written permission.'
The parenthetical is decisive — it is not limited to maps. This repo commits its data files,
so BONAP can INFORM a value but cannot BE one.
=> County nativity has NO redistributable source. That is plan-shaping, not an obstacle to
route around: either ask BONAP for written permission (costs an email, non-commercial
project, would unblock the epic's headline field), or define the plantable set without it.
nl-41o.7's call.
Access note: bonap.org/bonap.net are HTTP-ONLY; HTTPS is refused, so any tool that
silently upgrades reports the site as DOWN rather than as restricted.

iNATURALIST IS NOT THE ALTERNATIVE, and the negative result is the valuable part.
- establishment_means does NOT work: /v1/taxa/{id}?place_id=1281 does not filter, and the
  listed_taxa are sparse and idiosyncratic (Israel, Carson City, a Williamson County park).
  NO Dallas County listing exists for any species tried.
- The cultivated:wild observation ratio looked like a discriminator and then FAILED ITS OWN
  TEST. Dallas County (place_id 1281), research-grade wild vs captive:
    Lagerstroemia indica  2 wild / 594 captive = 297.0   (planted-only exotic; high end)
    Chilopsis linearis   52 / 147 = 2.83                 (the species we want excluded)
    Quercus shumardii   240 /  59 = 0.25
    Prunus mexicana     332 /  49 = 0.15
    NANDINA DOMESTICA  1033 / 111 = 0.11  <-- INVASIVE, on our own dfw-avoid-non-natives.csv
    Packera obovata     282 /  16 = 0.06
    Solanum elaeag.     488 /   1 = 0.00  (weedy native; low end)
    Ambrosia trifida   1989 /   0 = 0.00  (weedy native; low end)
  The first four were picked knowing the answer; the last four were added to bracket the
  range from cases NOT picked for effect, and that is what exposed the flaw.
  => The ratio measures NATURALIZATION, not NATIVITY. Nandina scores BETTER than Shumard
  oak because it genuinely escapes across DFW. A nativity filter built on this would admit
  one of the region's worst invasive shrubs. No threshold can fix that — and picking one
  would be exactly the invented weight this project rejected for the composite score and
  for FQA. NO THRESHOLD PROPOSED; admissibility is nl-41o.7's call.

JOIN KEY: USDA SYMBOL, with the numeric USDA Id carried alongside as the API access key.
Argued from three independent sources, not asserted: (1) NPIN keys on it IN ITS URL
(result.php?id_plant=PRME), so the two best sources join for free with no name matching;
(2) usda_symbol is already 100% populated in both draft CSVs (469/469, 61/61); (3) it is
stable, public, and USDA's licensing is unrestricted, so the key is not encumbered.
FOUR namespaces are in play — USDA symbols, Kartesz names (BONAP), iNat taxon ids, GBIF
usageKey. GBIF /species/match is the only automated cross-walk measured working.
CANNOT ADDRESS CULTIVARS: no botanical database indexes them (checked USDA, NPIN, BONAP,
GBIF). A cultivar can inherit species-level facts, but the traits that make it worth
choosing are exactly the ones that do NOT inherit — 'Nana' is a 3ft dwarf where the species
reaches 45ft, and height feeds rule 11. Needs a first-class cultivar row that inherits by
default and overrides explicitly, with overrides carrying their own provenance (nl-41o.4).

FIELDS NO SOURCE COVERS — exactly two, failing for different reasons:
  mature width    genuinely unpublished (absent from USDA's 81 chars AND from NPIN) -> books
  county nativity a LICENSING problem, not a data problem -> BONAP permission, or do without

NOT ASSESSED: Texas A&M AgriLife. Recorded as unassessed rather than guessed at; NPIN
already covers its plausible fields, so it is a low-priority follow-up, not a gap.
NPIN (LBJ Wildflower Center) IS THE BIG UNDER-RATED SOURCE, and it REVERSES three
verdicts from nl-41o.1. Measured on CHLI2, QUSH, ILVO, PRME:
- Reachable by plain curl WITH A BROWSER USER-AGENT — all three returned HTTP 200 with full
  content. The blanket 'behind Cloudflare' reading is WRONG: species pages serve normally
  while /robots.txt, /terms, /copyright, /privacy and /collections/ are challenged or 403.
- TERMS ARE UNREAD, and that IS the finding — the terms page is the unreachable one. Did NOT
  attempt to work around the protection. Verdict: 'usable, rate-unknown, terms-unread'.
  The honest route is to email the Center, not to probe harder.
- Keyed by USDA SYMBOL directly in the URL (result.php?id_plant=PRME).
- Publishes, per species: Bloom Time BY MONTH ('Feb, Mar, Apr' — beats USDA's season words);
  LIGHT REQUIREMENT AS A SET ('Sun, Part Shade, Shade' for Ilex vomitoria); Water Use; Soil
  Description + Soil Moisture set; CaCO3/cold/heat tolerance; Commercially Avail; DEER
  RESISTANT; LARVAL HOST as prose ('Henrys Elfin butterfly'); Nectar Source; Attracts;
  propagation. NO WIDTH — 'Size Notes' is height only.

THREE CORRECTIONS APPLIED TO docs/data-acquisition/01-... in the same commit:
1. nl-41o.1 said light tolerance breadth 'does not exist at any source' and R8's light check
   'stays a point check forever'. WRONG AS STATED — true of USDA, false of NPIN. R8's light
   row becomes fixable-if-NPIN-is-reachable-at-volume: an ACCESS question, not a source gap.
2. nl-41o.1 said species-level insect association data does not exist. TOO BROAD — no API
   publishes it (PlantPollinator is empty, measured), but NPIN curates it per species as
   text. So R5 is partial but NOT PERMANENTLY so; its ceiling is extraction, not sourcing.
3. nl-41o.1 ruled deer resistance OUT for 'no authoritative source'. REVERSED — NPIN
   publishes it as a structured field. Now a value judgement, reopened for nl-41o.7.
UNCHANGED: mature width is absent from NPIN too, confirming nl-41o.3's book corpus is the
sole route and the bead that un-defers rules 9 and 12.

OTHER SOURCES:
- USDA PLANTS: PRIMARY. US Gov work -> public domain, cleanest licensing here. Keep the
  self-imposed 1 req/s.
- GBIF: CORROBORATING, and its real value is STRUCTURAL — it returns a machine-readable
  per-record and per-dataset 'license' field (iNat research-grade = CC BY-NC 4.0). Since
  BONAP proves the store must answer 'may this value be published?' PER VALUE, nl-41o.4
  should model licence as a first-class property of a claim. At least one real source
  already emits it. establishmentMeans was undefined on the record sampled, so GBIF is not
  a shortcut to nativity either.
- NWF keystone PDF: still reachable (HTTP 200, 371750 bytes). Genus x ecoregion. Unchanged.
- NPSOT: the CLEANEST access permission of any source — robots.txt returns 200 and
  explicitly permits plant profiles with Crawl-delay: 10, disallowing only admin/search/
  event paths. The only source that states a machine-readable rate.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pre-indexed document corpus: books, PDFs, and citation
description:
Native plant books and regional PDFs hold a lot of what no API publishes —
local horticultural judgement, tolerance ranges, wildlife value, propagation.
Sized separately from the web sources because the mechanics differ completely:
acquisition, OCR or text extraction, chunking, retrieval, and citing back to a
page rather than a URL.

Analysis, not implementation. What is the corpus, how does a claim from page 214
of a book become a sourced field value, and what does the citation look like
when the source is not linkable?
design:
QUESTIONS TO ANSWER:

  Corpus     Which books and PDFs, and are they legitimately in hand? A scanned
             copyrighted book is a licensing question before it is a technical
             one. Distinguish FACT EXTRACTION (a soil tolerance is a fact, not
             expression) from reproducing text — the first is defensible, the
             second is not, and the pipeline must not store or emit long
             excerpts.
  Extraction pdftotext -layout already proved itself on the NWF keystone PDF and
             also proved the hazard: a two-column layout silently DROPPED Alnus
             from the caterpillar list, and only a second pass caught it (see
             AGENTS.md). Assume every layout lies until checked. Scanned books
             need OCR and OCR makes errors that look like data.
  Chunking   Species-keyed, not page-keyed — a species account may span pages,
             and a page may cover several species.
  Retrieval  How is the right passage found for a given species x field? Full
             text index, embeddings, or a hand-built species-to-page map?
  Citation   A URL is checkable; "page 214" is not, from the app. Decide what a
             book-sourced value's `source` string carries — edition, ISBN,
             page — so a human can verify it later.
  Confidence A book's judgement and a USDA field are not the same kind of claim.
             This feeds the conflict-resolution bead.

CARRY OVER the host-genera.csv rule: a value that cannot be sourced stays blank.
An OCR pass that is 90% right is 10% invented data, which is worse than absent.
acceptance_criteria:
• A named corpus with a licensing verdict per item, and a stated boundary
  between extracting facts and reproducing text
• An extraction approach with a verification step, given the Alnus precedent
• A citation format for non-linkable sources, decided
• A recommendation on retrieval, with the reasoning
notes:
FOLLOW-UP MEASUREMENT, same session -- the first pass did NOT test the inference
the epic depends on. The controls showed the prose FIRES when present, and that
known NCTX natives are silent (41/41). Neither tests the CONVERSE: that silence
implies native. The 41 positives genuinely are NCTX natives, so their silence is
consistent with the rule without testing it.

Tested properly against the at-risk population -- species native to the
continental U.S. but NOT to NCTX, present as cultivated escapes, which
self-identify in the prose:
  199 treatments use escape/cultivation language
  174 also carry `I` or an origin statement
   25 do NOT  ->  THE SILENCE INFERENCE LEAKS AT 12.6%

NOT a tuning problem. The flora writes "native IN rocky woods of Edwards
Plateau" -- adding `in` to the regex recovers only 2 of 25 (12.6% -> 11.6%).
The residual 23 carry the signal in the DISTRIBUTION SENTENCE instead:
  Ilex vomitoria      "naturalized in Dallas and Tarrant cos.; mainly se, e,
                       and sc Texas"
  Hesperaloe parviflora "otherwise mostly much further w in sw TX"
Reading a range is a materially harder extraction than matching a phrase, and
is the only route to county-level rather than region-level nativity. Unscoped.

REVISED DESIGN -- closes the leak by ROUTING, not by classifying:
  1. `I` symbol                  -> introduced
  2. "native of/from/to/IN ..."  -> review
  3. ESCAPE/CULTIVATION LANGUAGE -> review, EVEN WITH NO ORIGIN PHRASE
  4. otherwise                   -> native by silence
Screen (3) is the one a reasonable implementation would omit; it exists only
because the converse was tested. By construction it covers the whole at-risk
population.

MEASURED COST, small enough for human review:
  plants.csv (47):                     36 silence / 6 review / 0 I / 5 unknown
  blackland-prairie-natives.csv (469): 323 / 23 / 4 / 119
close_reason: Delivered docs/data-acquisition/03-document-corpus.md. Nativity convention verified against both control sets; three extraction bugs found and fixed; width claim corrected.

title: Goals analysis: what data gauges fitness for Dallas County
description:
Work BACKWARDS from the questions the app must answer to a field-by-field
requirement spec. Collection scoped by anything else will gather a lot of data
that answers nothing.

Deliverable: a table of required fields. For each — which question consumes it,
what granularity is needed (county / ecoregion / state), what provenance is
acceptable, and whether a blank is tolerable or disqualifying.

Then the honest half: an AVAILABILITY audit. For each required field, does a
credible source publish it at the needed granularity at all? Some will not
exist, and the plan must say so rather than leave a column to be filled in by
guesswork later. That answer determines which ecology rules are ever fully
computable and which stay partial forever.
design:
KNOWN CONSUMERS as of 2026-08-27 — start here, but do not stop here; the point
is to ask what fitness assessment NEEDS, not only what today's six rules use.

Shipped rules (src/analysis/rules/):
  6  bloom succession   flowering months
  7  bird food          fruit months, fruit load
  11 vertical layers    height, growth shape
  4/10 keystone genera  genus, LOCAL insect associations, width (footprint area)
  5  larval hosts       genus, documented host relationships
  8  site match         sun/water/soil REQUIREMENT and TOLERANCE (tolerance absent today)

Deferred (nl-jsm.7): rule 9 drifts, rule 12 mature-size spacing — both want
mature width and spread habit.

Suggestion ranking needs everything above PLUS availability in the nursery
trade, or the panel recommends species nobody can buy.

FIELDS KNOWN MISSING, with a candidate source already identified:
  nativity at COUNTY granularity     USDA PLANTS county distribution; BONAP
  soil/light/water TOLERANCE breadth USDA soil_coarse/medium/fine, shade_tolerance,
                                     drought_tolerance, moisture_use — already in
                                     blackland-prairie-natives.csv
  local insect associations          harder; NWF is genus x ecoregion only

QUESTIONS WORTH ASKING that today's rules do not:
  - Is this species commercially available near Dallas?
  - Is it aggressive or a reseeder that will take the bed?
  - Deer resistance, toxicity, allergen load — fitness for a FRONT yard
  - Bloom COLOR and structure for specialist bees, not just bloom timing
  - Nectar vs pollen value; host-plant specificity
  - Longevity and whether it needs division
Decide explicitly which are in scope. Each one added is a column to source for
several hundred species.

OPEN QUESTION worth resolving early: is 'fitness' one score or a profile? The
nl-jsm epic already decided AGAINST a composite score for the ecology check
because the weights would be invented. The same argument probably applies here.
acceptance_criteria:
• A required-fields table: field, consuming question, needed granularity,
  acceptable provenance, blank-tolerable yes/no
• An availability verdict per field, naming a real source or stating plainly
  that none publishes it at that granularity
• An explicit in/out scope list for the candidate new questions above
• A decision on whether fitness is a score or a profile, with the reasoning
notes:
Interleaves with nl-41o.9. The required-fields half can be written from the known consumers with no tooling; the AVAILABILITY half is far better answered by probing a source than by reading its documentation. Expect to alternate rather than finish one then the other.
DELIVERABLE: docs/data-acquisition/01-goals-and-required-fields.md (new docs/ tree).
Every claim in it is marked MEASURED or BELIEF.

HEADLINE FINDING (measured 2026-08-27), which amends this epic's premise:
USDA DOES publish county-level distribution, machine-readable. tools/usda-plants/
README.md says 'There is no distribution endpoint in the API (all 42 paths checked)'
— that is WRONG. The endpoint is misleadingly named and reads as a docs download:
  POST /api/PlantProfile/getDownloadDistributionDocumentation  {"masterId": <plantId>}
returns text/csv: Symbol,Country,State,State FIP,County,County FIP.
Verified: Quercus shumardii 682 rows / 27 TX counties / present in Dallas Co (48113).
Note {"unfilteredPlantIds":[id]} returns headers only — masterId is the working key.
State-level rows (empty County) come back mixed in and must be split on parse.

BUT — the same probe shows county NATIVITY is still unsourced. The CSV has exactly six
columns and NO native/adventive flag; it records PRESENCE only. Desert willow
(Chilopsis linearis, 49196) appears in Dallas County EXACTLY as Mexican plum
(Prunus mexicana, 90602) does, because it is widely planted here. So county presence
alone does NOT resolve the epic's own worked example.
=> The 'highest-leverage single field' is really TWO fields: presence (SOLVED, free,
US Gov) and nativity (UNSOLVED, BONAP the only candidate, and the blocker is LICENSING
not access — a question for nl-41o.2).
=> Still a real win: a COUNTY-RESTRICTED keystone count is now computable, narrowing
keystoneGenera.js's disclaimer from 'anywhere in the Great Plains' to 'recorded in this
county'.

DECIDED: fitness is a PROFILE, not a score. A composite would have to weigh data
quality against plant quality, which are not commensurable — a great species with one
missing field would score like a mediocre species with complete data. No fitness column.

SCOPE RULING on the candidate questions — IN (free, already in the USDA response):
commercial availability, toxicity, spread/reseed risk, lifespan, fruit persistence.
IN (expensive, load-bearing): mature width. OUT: deer resistance (no authoritative
source — sourcing it means inventing data), allergen load (proprietary, no consumer),
bloom colour/structure for specialist bees (needs a bee-to-trait mapping we lack),
nectar-vs-pollen value, needs-division.
SECOND ROUND OF MEASUREMENTS (2026-08-27), closing the availability audit:

SPECIES-LEVEL INSECT DATA DOES NOT EXIST — now MEASURED, not believed.
/api/PlantPollinator/{id} exists in swagger and would have been the fix for the keystone
attribution problem (species-level, where NWF is genus x ecoregion). It returns [] for
EVERY species tried, including the strongest positive controls: Asclepias asperula
(43487), Asclepias viridis (43632), Passiflora incarnata (69379), Salix nigra (68068),
Quercus shumardii (70468). If milkweed has no pollinator record, nothing does.
=> The plan should STOP treating a species-level insect signal as something a probe might
still turn up. This makes rules 5 and 4/10 PERMANENTLY partial — a property of the
domain, not a backlog item (see nl-41o.6).

/api/PlantWildlife/{id} IS populated, unlike its pollinator sibling. 13 species sampled:
6/6 woody fruiting (Ilex vomitoria, Callicarpa americana, Juniperus virginiana, Celtis
laevigata, Rhus glabra, Morus rubra), 0/2 for Prunus mexicana and Quercus stellata,
0/4 herbaceous. Coarse Minor/Low/Moderate forage values for Large/Small Mammals, Water
and Terrestrial Birds. TerrestrialBirds is a DOCUMENTED forage value — a stronger and
independent signal for rule 7, which today infers bird food from a month range plus
fruit_load. Corroboration, not a primary field.

/api/PlantSynonyms/{id} answers the identity problem — see nl-41o.4.

ADDED to the doc: a full per-field verdict table (all 18 fields, matching the
required-fields numbering) and a RULE COMPUTABILITY table, which the bead body asked for
and the first draft only gestured at. Headline: three of six shipped rules are fully
computable today or nearly so — the data gap is NARROWER than the epic assumed, because
county presence and soil tolerance both turned out to be in hand. Two dimensions (R5,
R4/R10) stay partial forever. R8 splits: soil fixable now, water derivable, light
permanently a point check.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plant data acquisition: analysis and planning
description:
Design a system that builds high-quality, county-scoped plant data for North
Central Texas, so the ecology checks can gauge the fitness of EVERY relevant
species for Dallas County rather than grading against 48 hand-entered rows.

This epic is ANALYSIS AND PLANNING ONLY. No collection is built here; the
output is a set of decisions and specs the implementation epic is written from.

Expected shape of the system (from the user, 2026-08-27): pre-indexed documents
(native plant books), web crawlers, and some manual correction. Because the data
volume is large, the plan has to cover access, prioritization, collection, data
modeling and indexing, quality measures and metrics, and conflict/correction
resolution — plus a goals analysis of what information is even available, and
MCP tooling that lets an agent introspect the processing as it runs.
design:
WHY NOW — four findings from the nl-jsm ecology epic, each traced to a data gap:

1. CONTINENTAL NATIVITY IS USELESS HERE. The draft CSVs carry
   usda_native_status, whose values are 'L48:N' and 'CAN:N|L48:N' — native to
   the lower 48. Desert willow (Chilopsis linearis, West Texas) and Mexican plum
   (Prunus mexicana, Blackland Prairie) therefore score IDENTICALLY, though one
   is in a genus hosting 222 caterpillar species locally and the other is out of
   range. plants.csv has no nativity column at all. The needed granularity is
   COUNTY, not continent.

2. KEYSTONE COUNTS CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO A SPECIES. NWF counts are per GENUS
   per ECOREGION. Packera obovata qualifies solely via synonym_of -> Senecio's
   22 pollen-specialist bees, most of which rely on Senecio/Packera species that
   do not occur near Dallas. With county-level occurrence we could compute a
   LOCAL keystone count instead of importing an ecoregion-wide one. Same data
   gap as (1).

3. NO TOLERANCE DATA, ONLY PREFERENCE. plants.csv soil_pref/sun_pref/water_pref
   each hold ONE preferred value, so rule 8 cannot tell "will not grow" from
   "grows, just smaller". Mitigated for now by demoting soil to a caution
   (commit a93ed52) — a stopgap, not a fix. USDA already publishes the breadth:
   usda_soil_coarse/medium/fine, usda_shade_tolerance, usda_drought_tolerance,
   usda_moisture_use are all present in blackland-prairie-natives.csv.

4. COVERAGE. plants.csv is 48 species; blackland-prairie-natives.csv is 469.
   Every suggestion the panel makes is bounded by the catalog, so thin coverage
   caps the usefulness of every rule, not just one.

PRIOR ART IN THE TREE — review before designing anything. Eight untracked
root-level CSVs look like this work roughly 70% done:
  blackland-prairie-natives.csv   469 rows, 49 columns incl. USDA fields
  dfw-nctx-natives.csv            62 rows
  dfw-avoid-non-natives.csv       13 rows
  dfw-already-in-plants-csv.csv
  texas-usda-plants.csv
  dfw-needs-manual-data.txt       ~12 species the automated pass could not fill
  dfw-plant-list-names.txt, blackland-prairie-species-names.txt
There are also usda-plants MCP tools wired into the session
(usda_search_by_location, usda_search_by_name, usda_fetch_details,
usda_download_plant_list) and a tools/ directory.

DISCIPLINE TO CARRY OVER from ecology/host-genera.csv (nl-jsm.1): every derived
value carries a source, and anything unverifiable stays BLANK rather than
guessed. AGENTS.md: don't invent plant data. That rule is what makes the
resulting confidence metrics mean anything.
notes:
Filed 2026-08-27 after the nl-jsm ecology epic shipped. The user asked to step back into a new session for this thinking; these beads are the agenda for it.
SCOPE CARVE-OUT (2026-08-27): the epic is analysis and planning, with ONE exception — nl-41o.9 builds a working source-probe MCP tool early, because nl-41o.1 and nl-41o.2 have to measure what sources actually publish rather than trust their documentation. The tool is read-only and cannot write to any data file. All other collection is a later epic.
TOOLING DECIDED 2026-08-27 (user, in session):
- STORE: SQLite, WAL mode, at data/claims.db. Chosen over DuckDB on WRITE PATTERN
  (point inserts + single-row correction UPDATEs, not bulk-load-then-scan) and
  CONCURRENCY (nl-41o.8 needs introspection to read while a collection pass writes;
  DuckDB is single-writer/single-process). Size does not discriminate: ~500 species
  x ~40 fields x 3-5 sources is only 60-100k rows, milliseconds in either engine.
  SQLite is also stdlib in Python AND built into Node 26 (node:sqlite verified) —
  zero dependency on both sides of the language split. DuckDB was offered as an
  ad-hoc CSV query tool and DECLINED; not installed.
  Postgres rejected (a service for 100k rows); bare Parquet/JSONL rejected (no point
  updates, which kills corrections).
- LANGUAGE: Node stays the core — the claim store, the probe, and the MCP surface —
  because .mcp.json runs Node, tools/usda-plants already encodes hard-won USDA
  knowledge (the shade-tolerance inversion, the timeout endpoint), and nl-41o.8
  names 'two servers with overlapping vocabulary' as the bad outcome. Python is
  added ONLY for nl-41o.3's PDF/OCR work, writing into the same SQLite file — a
  clean process boundary at a real capability gap.
- COMMITTED ARTIFACTS: data/claims.db is GITIGNORED and rebuildable. Only the
  exported plants.csv and a plain-text manual-corrections file are committed, so a
  researched correction is reviewable in a diff and survives any rebuild.
- The app never learns SQLite: plants.csv stays a flat file the browser fetches,
  generated as an export from the claim store.

title: Rule 8: match plants to declared site conditions
description:
src/analysis/rules/siteMatch.js - compare each species' sunPref/waterPref/soilPref against the project's site block.

Catalog vocabularies: sun full-sun|part-sun|shade, water low|medium, soil clay|clay-loam|loamy|sandy. Soil is set membership. Sun and water are ordered scales.
design:
READ THIS BEFORE WRITING THE COMPARATOR - the direction has been wrong here once.

sun_pref is a light REQUIREMENT, not a shade tolerance. Commit ed9d75c ('Fix inverted
sun_pref: Low/Medium/High is light requirement') fixed exactly this inversion: little
bluestem, Indiangrass and switchgrass are full-sun (high light requirement), Carex
blanda and inland sea oats are shade (low).

So the comparison is ASYMMETRIC, not a distance:
- plant needs MORE light than the site gives -> real failure (won't bloom, will flop);
  flag at one step, hard at two
- plant needs LESS light than the site gives -> scorch risk; mild at one step (a
  part-sun plant in a full-sun yard is usually fine), real at two (a shade sedge in
  full sun)

water_pref is likewise a requirement: a high plant on a low-water site droughts out, a
low plant on a high-water site rots. Both directions are findings, but they are
DIFFERENT findings and the copy must say which.

Put a comment in the rule module pointing at ed9d75c so the next reader doesn't
re-invert it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests cover BOTH directions on sun and on water, not just one
- A project with no site block reports not-declared rather than throwing
- Soil accepts the single value plants.csv uses
close_reason: Closed

title: Rules 4/10 keystone genera and 5 larval hosts
description:
src/analysis/rules/{keystoneGenera,larvalHosts}.js - join the placed genera to ecology/host-genera.csv.

Rule 4/10: report which keystone genera are present, and the share of planted FOOTPRINT AREA (pi*(width/2)^2) sitting in keystone genera - rule 10 is about space and budget, not head-count. Suggest unplanted catalog species in keystone genera.

Rule 5: at least one placed genus with a non-empty larval_hosts or lep_host_species. Name the hosts found; suggest catalog additions when none.
design:
WIDTH DEFAULT TRAP: createPlantFromSpecies defaults width ?? 1, so a species with a
blank width_ft silently contributes 1 sq ft of footprint. Harmless for a perennial,
badly wrong if a tree lands with a blank width. EXCLUDE plants with no declared width
from BOTH sides of the area ratio, and say how many were excluded.

Rule 5 must NOT be derived from keystone membership alone. The frontyard's Asclepias
asperula is a monarch host and Asclepias is not on either NWF top-30 list - deriving
rule 5 from keystone genera would score that design as having no larval host, which is
plainly wrong. That is exactly why host-genera.csv carries a separate larval_hosts
column (nl-jsm.1).
acceptance_criteria:
EXPECT A BAD SCORE, and that is correct, not a bug:
Only 5 of the catalog's 42 genera are keystone in ecoregion 9 - Helianthus, Solidago,
Symphyotrichum, Verbesina, Vernonia - and NONE are woody (no Quercus, Prunus, Salix).
Both projects will report weak on 4/10. The panel copy must read as a gap to close,
not as an error.

- Packera obovata resolves through synonym_of to Senecio and counts (frontyard has 3)
- Asclepias asperula satisfies rule 5 for the frontyard
- A project with no ecoregion reports not-declared
close_reason: Closed

title: Declare ecoregion and site in project.json
description:
Rules 8 and 4/10 need inputs nothing declares today.

  "ecoregion": "9",
  "site": { "sun": "part-sun", "water": "medium", "soil": "clay" }

Thread through src/data/projectConfig.js and set both for the two existing projects.
design:
SILENT-DROP HAZARD: serializeProjectConfig WHITELISTS fields. A field added only to
normalizeProjectConfig survives in memory but is dropped the first time Setup mode
saves the project - the user's declaration vanishes with no error. Both functions must
be updated, and tests/projectConfig.test.js needs a round-trip assertion that
site/ecoregion survive normalize -> serialize.

Both fields optional: a project without them reports not-declared on rules 8 and 4/10
rather than throwing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round-trip test: normalize then serialize keeps site and ecoregion
- A project.json with neither field still loads and renders
- Both projects/*/project.json carry real values
close_reason: Closed

title: Ecology check panel in the UI
description:
src/render/ecologyPanel.js plus the markup, styles, and app.js hook. Makes rules 6/7/11 visible end to end before the harder rules land.

- index.html: <div class="ecology-check" id="ecologyCheck"> immediately above .species-table, collapse toggle following the settings-drawer pattern
- renderEcologyPanel(results, container): one row per dimension - status chip, one-line summary, expandable body with findings and suggestions, mirroring the species table's existing Details disclosure
- styles.css
- src/app.js: load + hook
design:
TWO HAZARDS, both already documented in the code:

1. Hook into refreshSpeciesTable (src/app.js ~line 318), NOT render(). The comment
   there is explicit about why: render() fires on every month-slider input event, and
   rebuilding this DOM mid-drag would orphan the row the closure is holding.

2. Load ecology/host-genera.csv with fetchCsv alongside plants.csv in the Promise.all
   at src/app.js:1171. A failure to load it must degrade the three genus-dependent
   rules to not-declared, NOT break the app.

Panel maps exactly the four statuses from nl-jsm.2 - no ad-hoc chips.
acceptance_criteria:
- npm run test:e2e spec asserting the panel renders and expands
- MUST add the project the spec targets to SCRATCH_PROJECTS in tests-e2e/scratch-fixture.mjs. A spec pointed at a project missing from that list silently falls back to drag-plan and asserts against the wrong yard (see the stored memory on this - it fails misleadingly, not loudly)
- No inline style on any view SVG (three controllers already share those elements)
close_reason: Closed

title: Rules engine + rules 6, 7, 11 (no new data needed)
description:
src/analysis/ecology.js registry plus the three rules computable from data already in plants.csv. Pure modules, no DOM.

- src/analysis/ecology.js - analyzeEcology(ctx) -> one result per rule
- src/analysis/rules/{bloomSuccession,birdFood,verticalLayers}.js - each exports { id, title, evaluate(ctx) }
- src/utils/speciesKey.js - add getGenus(plant) sibling to getSpeciesKey
- tests/ecology.test.js
design:
Result shape: { id, title, status, summary, findings[], suggestions[] }

status is a CLOSED SET OF FOUR - no other value, the panel maps exactly four chips:
  ok            nothing to do
  partial       works, has a hole
  gap           dimension essentially unmet
  not-declared  the input this rule needs is absent

ctx is built once: { plants, species, hostGenera, site, ecoregion }. plants are the
objects createPlantFromSpecies already mints - the analysis must NEVER build its own
plant shape (AGENTS.md: two builders would let the paths drift).

REUSE, don't reimplement:
- classifyPlantLayer (src/state/layers.js) for rule 11. It already buckets
  trees/sculptural/accents/groundcover. Do not re-bucket by height.
- plant.floweringMonths / plant.fruitMonths from plantParser. addRange there already
  wraps via modulo, so fruit_season_months '10-2' yields {10,11,12,1,2}. Wrap-around
  comes for free; just don't reimplement month parsing.

Rule 6 bloom succession: species count per month. Target window = union of the placed
plants' growingMonths (data-driven, so no hardcoded Texas season). Zero-bloom months
inside that window are gaps; one-species months are thin.

Rule 7 bird food: species count per month from fruitMonths, weighted by fruitLoad,
emphasizing Sep-Feb. Suggestions rank catalog species by how much of the gap they cover.

Rule 11 vertical layers: counts per classifyPlantLayer bucket; an empty layer is a finding.

Suggestions come from plants.csv ONLY. The untracked regional CSVs
(blackland-prairie-natives.csv etc.) are out of scope - uncommitted and partly
unpopulated per dfw-needs-manual-data.txt.
acceptance_criteria:
Expected first-run results, verified against the real data during planning:
- Both projects: zero bloom Dec-Feb, only 1 species blooming in November
- example-frontyard: NO fruit at all Nov-May -> gap
- backyard: strong fruit (7 species in Oct, 2-4 through winter) -> ok
- example-frontyard layers: ground 3, mid 10, tall 4, canopy 0
- backyard layers: ground 38, mid 21, tall 4, canopy 1

Test that a wrap-around fruit range (10-2) counts as winter food.
tests/run-tests.cjs discovers by glob (readdir + .test.js/.test.cjs), so new test
files run automatically - no manifest to update.
close_reason: Closed

title: Build ecology/host-genera.csv from NWF ecoregion 9 keystone lists
description:
One genus-keyed reference table shared by rules 4, 5, and 10 - they all reduce to 'what does this genus do for insects'. Per-species columns on plants.csv were rejected: 48 rows of hand-researched booleans is expensive and invites invention.

Columns: genus,ecoregion,lep_host_species,bee_specialist_species,larval_hosts,synonym_of,source

Also: src/analysis/hostGenera.js to parse and index it (resolving synonym_of), plus tests/hostGenera.test.js.
design:
Source: NWF Keystone Native Plants, Great Plains - Ecoregion 9
https://www.nwf.org/-/media/Documents/PDFs/Garden-for-Wildlife/Keystone-Plants/NWF-GFW-keystone-plant-list-ecoregion-9-great-plains.pdf

Dallas / Blackland Prairie is EPA Level I ecoregion 9 (Great Plains) - verified, not assumed. Level III 32 Texas Blackland Prairies sits under Level I 9.

The PDF extracts cleanly with 'pdftotext -layout'. Two top-30 tables:

LEP HOST (caterpillar species supported), read verbatim:
Quercus 253, Prunus 222, Salix 214, Betula 189, Populus 180, Alnus 164, Malus 162,
Carya 153, Vaccinium 146, Acer 145, Pinus 145, Ulmus 109, Larix 99, Castanea 98,
Tsuga 92, Tilia 91, Crataegus 90, Juglans 89, Rubus 88, Fraxinus 86, Abies 85,
Corylus 76, Picea 75, Rosa 75, Pseudotsuga 74, Solidago 71, Amelanchier 69,
Cornus 65, Vitis 60, Helianthus 58

CAUTION: the two-column PDF layout interleaves the lep and bee tables, and wrapped
rows put the count on the FOLLOWING line (Prunus 222, Populus 180, Vaccinium 146).
Alnus 164 appears in the upper summary table but was dropped by a naive line-wise
extraction of the top-30 column. Re-verify the full 30 against the PDF before
committing - do not trust a single pass.

BEE SPECIALIST (pollen specialist bee species relying on it):
Helianthus 89, Grindelia 68 (printed 'Gridelia' - a typo in the PDF; use Grindelia
and note it in source), Solidago 56, Chrysothamnus 52, Gutierrezia 50,
Heterotheca 50, Symphyotrichum 43, Ericameria 41, Verbesina 34, Rudbeckia 32,
Cirsium 30, Erigeron 30, Machaeranthera 28, Coreopsis 27, Baileya 25, Senecio 22,
Salix 20, Gaillardia 18, Bidens 16, Isocoma 16, Baccharis 14, Ratibida 14,
Astragalus 13, Chrysopsis 13, Dalea 12, Heliomeris 12, Vernonia 12, Heliopsis 11,
Oenothera 11, Helenium 10

synonym_of is load-bearing: NWF lists Senecio, but the catalog and BOTH layouts use
Packera obovata (segregated from Senecio obovatus). Without the mapping the
frontyard's ragwort is silently missed.

larval_hosts covers well-documented obligate relationships the keystone lists miss -
Asclepias to monarch, Passiflora to gulf fritillary, native bunchgrasses to skippers.
These need sourcing during implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every row carries a source; a genus with nothing sourced stays BLANK rather than guessed (AGENTS.md: don't invent plant data)
- Keystone counts match the PDF verbatim, all 30 in each list, Alnus included
- hostGenera.js resolves synonym_of, so Packera resolves to Senecio's bee count
- ecoregion is a column, so a second region is a data change not a code change
- tests/hostGenera.test.js covers synonym resolution and a blank-count genus
close_reason: Closed

title: Ecological design feedback: per-dimension rules engine
description:
Grade a planting design against ecological rules and suggest fixes, reported per dimension with no composite score.

Plan: /home/johntron/.claude/plans/generic-meandering-hamming.md

Scope: rules 6 (bloom succession), 7 (bird food), 11 (vertical layers), 4/10 (keystone genera), 5 (larval hosts), 8 (site match).

Out of scope: FQA (wrong instrument - grades remnant intactness, and FQI rewards richness which contradicts the drift rules; no verified NCTX C-value list exists). Rules 14-16 are maintenance practices, not layout properties. Rules 9 and 12 are computable but deferred.

title: Position and scale a photo, without stretching it
description:
Photo positioning is deferred, not solved. The distortion is gone only because the gestures that caused it were removed: dragging a photo and scaling it from a measured length both wrote photoFt starting from the PANEL's rectangle when a photo had no placement, and the panel is the yard's shape, not the picture's — 4% off on backyard's 800x600, 39% on a 16:9 upload.

So a project can no longer be given a bad placement by hand, and placements already in a file still render (src/render/photoPlacement.js). What is missing is any way to create a good one.

Whatever replaces it needs the image's intrinsic aspect, which nothing currently loads. Storing photoFt at upload time from the decoded bitmap the upload path already holds would give every photo a real rectangle before it is ever touched; after that, drag and aspect-locked corner resize are both safe, and the user has asked for both. The ruler does not come back in its old form — under a declared yard it no longer solves a view's extent — though 'measure a known length to set the YARD' would be a genuinely useful tool.
close_reason: Closed

title: A shrunken yard strands the plants and features already outside it
description:
Setting yardFt smaller than the content in it leaves plants and features outside the yard with nothing saying so. Live right now in projects/example-frontyard, saved from the app at 6 x 25 ft: plant 'fournerve-edge' sits at (9.07, 9.08) and all three features reach past x 6 or y 25 — the box out to y 31.5. resolveYardBounds clamps NEW drags to the yard, so those cannot be dragged back; they draw outside it or not at all.

This is the half of the silent-shrink problem nl-t08 did not remove. It removed view-vs-view disagreement — no view can miss the yard now — but the yard itself is still a number a person can type below what is standing in it.

Fix: the Setup panel's yard section counts what falls outside the candidate yard on every edit, before Save, the way the old 'Shared yard' section reported the narrowing. Naming the plants is better than counting them. Refusing the edit is wrong — shrinking a yard you have not planted yet is normal.
close_reason: Closed

title: Features panel lists nothing until an edit: panel not re-rendered after async feature load
description: appState.features is assigned after loadProjectFeatures in src/app.js, but featurePanel.render() only ran earlier with an empty list. The shapes draw (render() follows), yet the Yard features list says 'Nothing drawn yet' until any commit re-renders the panel. Most visible on mobile, where the list is the main affordance.

title: example-frontyard's plan view is framed in a stale coordinate origin
description: The boot notice says view "west" covers y 0-14.3 ft while the plan covers 14.8-45.1 ft. nl-9j6 reported it and deliberately did not repair it. Evidence now settles which number is wrong: the plan's originFt {2, 14.833} is the outlier. Overlaying features.json's traced surface on the plan photo under a {0,0} origin puts it exactly on the dark bed; under {2, 14.833} it falls off the bottom of the photo entirely. All three elevations still carry originFt.x = 0 from the pre-photo 12x25 authoring, and the plants all sit at y = 14.833, the old bounds.y.min, i.e. clamped. Fix the plan's frame, and surface the shared yard live in Setup mode so a handle drag that reframes the plan cannot silently strand the elevations again.
acceptance_criteria: example-frontyard raises no yard conflict; Setup mode shows the resulting shared yard against the plan as the author edits; unit tests use inlined fixtures, never projects/.

The plan's originFt is now dropped (serializeProjectConfig omits {0,0}), elevation origins, features.json and planting_layout.csv untouched. Prevention: describeYardBounds() in src/render/yardBounds.js reports the shared yard, the plan's rectangle, and which view holds each differing edge; the Setup panel renders it under 'Shared yard' on every edit, in red when a view overlaps the plan nowhere — so the gesture that strands an elevation says so as it happens, not at next boot. 5 unit tests with inlined fixtures, including example-frontyard's own numbers. Residual narrowing filed separately.

description:
Switch src/render/topView.js, src/render/elevationViews.js, and src/interaction/dragController.js off the global pixelsPerInch and onto createViewTransform(view).

Dragging the Scale slider zooms panels while plants stay glued to the background photo. tests/topView.test.js and tests/elevationViews.test.js updated to the new signature; npm test and npm run test:e2e pass.

title: Config-driven view panels (no more hardcoded topView/frontView/sideView)
description:
The three panel names are baked in at more sites than the SVG refs:
  - index.html: #topSvg / #frontSvg / #sideSvg, data-view-panel='topView|frontView|sideView'
  - src/app.js:63-77: svgRefs.elevationSvgs and labelRefs built from literals
  - styles.css:779-781 and 1089-1091: maximize rules ENUMERATE all three names
  - configureViews / renderViews: positional mapping

Add a <template> to index.html, cloned once per views[] entry inside configureViews (already idempotent pure attribute/style assignment). renderViews loops views[] dispatching on type to renderTopView / renderElevationView. Keep id='topSvg' on the first plan view so existing e2e selectors keep working.

Maximize rules collapse to a generic .views[data-maximized] .view-panel.is-maximized, with refreshMaximizedView toggling the class; the data-maximized attribute stays for the container-level rules at styles.css 771/775/1100.
acceptance_criteria: A project.json declaring four views renders four panels, each maximizable. Backyard's three views look unchanged. Live preview works without a page reload: mutating appState.project then re-calling configureViews + render() is sufficient. npm run test:e2e passes.
close_reason: Panels are cloned from a <template> once per views[] entry; configureViews reconciles by view id so unchanged panels keep their SVG. Maximize CSS collapsed to .view-panel.is-maximized in both the desktop and mobile blocks. renderViews loops panels dispatching on type. Verified a 4-view project renders 4 maximizable panels against a scratch PUBLIC_DIR server; npm test and e2e 10/10 green.

title: views[] schema, legacy migration, and serializeProjectConfig
description:
Replace project.json's {plan, elevations[]} with a views[] array whose geometry is authored in feet.

Each view: { id, type: 'plan'|'elevation', viewFrom?, label, sublabel, viewBox {width,height}, originFt {x,y}, extentFt {width,height}, background|null, backgroundFrom? }

originFt is the yard coordinate at the viewBox bottom-left. On an elevation it replaces both pixel offsets: leftOffsetPx 80 -> originFt.x = -80/pxPerFt; bottomOffsetPx 100 -> originFt.y = -100/pxPerFt.

normalizeProjectConfig accepts BOTH shapes; legacy migrates with pxPerFt = defaultPixelsPerInch * 12. Writes always emit views[]. ELEVATION_SLOTS=2 goes away.

New serializeProjectConfig(config) omits values equal to defaults — normalizeProjectConfig inflates labels, sublabels and offsets, so writing the normalized object straight back would bloat every project file.

normalizeAssetPath currently THROWS on a missing background; relax it to allow null so a newly added view is valid before its image exists. Add the matching consumer branch in configureViews in the same commit — it sets container.style.backgroundImage unconditionally and would request projects/<slug>/null.
acceptance_criteria: pxPerFt = viewBox.width/extentFt.width must match viewBox.height/extentFt.height within tolerance; non-uniform views are rejected with a clear message. Path-traversal guard on background still holds. tests/projectConfig.test.js covers legacy->views[] migration, new-shape round-trip through serialize+normalize, default omission, and the validation errors; the /exactly 2 elevations/ assertion is removed.
close_reason: views[] schema + legacy migration + serializeProjectConfig landed. normalizeProjectConfig reads both shapes and also emits a derived legacy projection (plan/elevations/pixelsPerInch) so the app keeps working until nl-tz7.3/nl-tz7.4 rewire consumers. npm test (14 files) and npm run test:e2e (10 tests) both green.

The amlegal deep link (codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/dallas/latest/dallas_tx/0-0-0-108657) is a JS app that did not render the section text on fetch. title: SURFACE 1 (quick win): a rights page, quoting the statute
description:
Ships first: state law is uniform, fully verified, and needs no per-project data.

Content = the verified block in the parent issue. Quote 202.007(a)(4) and (d-1) verbatim - the actual words are more persuasive than any paraphrase, and a homeowner can hand them to a board.
MUST also state the limits, or the page sets people up to lose an argument: (c), (d)(4) gravel/rocks/cacti, (d)(5) maintenance, (d)(8) plan-submission, and the (e) carve-out.
